speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing the vision changes and black spots in your right eye? Are you currently taking antiretroviral therapy, and do you know your most recent CD4 count?

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of decreased vision and seeing black spots in the right eye. He reports no pain, and the left eye is asymptomatic. He mentions being treated for fungal esophagitis 6 months ago and was diagnosed with Kaposi's sarcoma 2 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of advanced AIDS and prior opportunistic infections, I need to know your current CD4 count and whether you are currently adherent to antiretroviral therapy. Have you experienced any floaters, flashes of light, or a shadow in your peripheral vision recently? REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy: Granular yellow-white opacities around the retinal vessels and multiple areas of dot-blot hemorrhages. CD4 Count: 36/mm3.

speaker: Doctor
text: The fundoscopic findings of granular yellow-white opacities and hemorrhages, combined with your critically low CD4 count of 36/mm³, are highly indicative of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis. To confirm this diagnosis and rule out other opportunistic infections, I will now review detailed retinal imaging. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Decreased vision and black spots in the right eye. I also have No pain, Left eye is asymptomatic.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of painless vision loss, floaters, and characteristic "pizza pie" retinal findings in a patient with advanced AIDS is diagnostic. DIAGNOSIS READY: Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis
